update.title: Turned watch activity into reusable sleep-session data
update.summary: Ported Gadgetbridge’s classification rules into a local Python tool that reads watch samples and returns reusable sleep sessions and daily activity totals.

preview.description: Keep device-specific decoding behind one data interface.

blocks.body:
## Read the watch data locally

I built Gadgetbridge Sleep to turn a synced watch database into data that other local tools can use. It reads activity samples from SQLite, classifies them, and produces sleep sessions and daily activity totals.

I replaced its external import dependency with a Python port of Gadgetbridge’s existing classification and aggregation algorithms. The tool owns the translation from device records to structured results; a dashboard can consume those results without reproducing the device rules.

blocks.code:
flowchart TB
 DB["Synced Gadgetbridge database"] --> TABLE{"Activity table"}
 TABLE --> MI["Mi Band: normalize flags and carry forward activity"]
 TABLE --> HU["Huami Extended: map explicit activity types"]
 MI --> SAMPLES["Classified samples"]
 HU --> SAMPLES
 SAMPLES --> SESSIONS["Sleep sessions"]
 SAMPLES --> TOTALS["Daily activity totals"]
 SESSIONS --> USE["Local consumers"]
 TOTALS --> USE
blocks.description: Two device-data paths converge on classified samples, which supply both session detection and daily totals.

blocks.body:
## Preserve the rules behind each sample

The two supported activity tables need different decoding paths. The Mi Band path strips flag bits and carries the previous valid activity type across “no change” samples. The Huami Extended path maps its explicit activity values directly.

I kept the corresponding Gadgetbridge Java sources alongside the port. That gives the Python implementation an inspectable reference for the behavior it carries across languages.

blocks.description: The Mi Band preprocessing loop preserves continuity by carrying a valid activity type across unchanged samples.

blocks.body:
## Return data that can be reused

Session detection and daily aggregation operate on the classified samples. The command-line interface exposes the results independently of the presentation layer, so the same local data can support a dashboard, an inspection command, or another integration.

The result connects a device-specific record format to a reusable Python data interface while retaining the upstream algorithm’s role in the implementation.
